bounded_statement: The report's selected result — a pooled two-sample Student t-test on all 48 coupon rows yielding t(46) = 23.465, p < 0.0001 — enters each declared independent unit (plate_id, 12 plates) four times into a procedure that assumes row independence. Because build_orientation is constant within a plate and the data show strong plate-level clustering (within-plate coupon range ~6 MPa versus between-plate mean spread ~16 MPa within an orientation), the effective independent sample size is 12 plates (df = 10), not 48 coupons (df = 46). The stated t-statistic, degrees of freedom, and p-value therefore overstate the evidence as reported. This finding is bounded to the validity of the stated inferential result: the direction and magnitude of the mean difference (40 MPa, edge > flat) are unaffected, and a correct plate-level t-test (t(10) ≈ 12.25) would still be significant at p < 0.0001.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report is transparent about the clustering: it discloses that the file contains 12 distinct build plates alongside 48 coupon rows, so the row-level design is not concealed. This mitigates concerns of misrepresentation but does not make the row-independent test valid.

counterevidence_considered.description: The effect is large enough that a correct plate-level analysis reaches the same qualitative conclusion: plate-mean groups (flat ≈ {296.5, 300.5, 304.5, 292.5, 308.5, 300.5}; edge ≈ {336.5, 340.5, 344.5, 332.5, 348.5, 340.5}, each SD ≈ 5.66) give t(10) ≈ 12.25, p < 0.0001. extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding three ways. (1) I searched the workflow for any aggregation to the declared independent unit before inference: uts_by_orientation iterates over raw rows and plate_id is only used to count distinct plates for display (workflow/analysis.py line 41); no per-plate averaging, mixed model, or cluster correction exists, so the test is genuinely row-level. (2) I checked whether rows might in fact be independent despite the declaration: the data contradict this — within-plate coupon values are tightly clustered (range ~6 MPa) while plate means within an orientation spread over ~16 MPa, indicating substantial intra-plate correlation, and build_orientation is constant within plate, so the between-group comparison has only 12 independent units. (3) I checked whether the reported numbers could correspond to a valid unit-level test: recomputing at the plate level gives t(10) ≈ 12.25, not the reported t(46) = 23.465, confirming the reported statistic comes from the pseudoreplicated row-level procedure. The qualitative conclusion survives correct analysis, but the stated statistical result does not, so the issue class is demonstrated and bounded accordingly.

root_cause: The workflow extracts tensile_strength_mpa from every coupon row per orientation (workflow/analysis.py uts_by_orientation) and passes these 24-per-group row-level values directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind with df = n1 + n2 - 2 = 46, without any aggregation to the declared independent unit plate_id. Each of the 12 plates contributes four correlated coupon measurements to a test that treats every entry as an independent observation, inflating the effective sample size fourfold and the degrees of freedom from 10 to 46.
